author: reek
body: `substring` traps on an out-of-range request. This file is the other half: every LEGAL request must still answer, including both boundaries, because a bounds check that refuses a legal call is worse than the hole it closed and `substring` is called from everywhere.

author: reek
body: The trap itself cannot be pinned here -- it is a UD2, so the guest dies and there is no output to compare. `codex/test/substring-over-read.codex` is that demonstration and it carries a `.fatal`, which means it is a compile check plus a manual read and nothing more. This file is the part a battery can actually fail on, so it is the one that has to be complete.

author: reek
body: The lattice is every start from 0 to the length, with every length that fits from that start. Zero length at every position is included, and so is the empty slice at the very end (start == length, length 0), which is the case a naive `start < length` check rejects.
